beats.text: Eisenhower never drew a box in his life.
Eisenhower quoted a line at the World Council of Churches: 'I have two kinds of problems, the urgent and the important. The urgent are not important, and the important are never urgent.'
beats.note: He credited it to 'a former college president', not to himself, and not by name.

beats.name: Dr J. Roscoe Miller
beats.role: Northwestern's president, who introduced Eisenhower that day and is named earlier in the speech. He is not the 'former college president' Eisenhower actually quotes, though most retellings assume he is.

beats.context: The gap between Eisenhower's speech and the year the four quadrant grid people picture was actually invented.

beats.name: Stephen Covey
beats.role: Turned Eisenhower's two sentences into the four quadrant grid in his book The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People, more than three decades after the speech.

beats.line: The quote is Eisenhower's. The box belongs to somebody else entirely.
